---
title: "fedscreen"
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
    # Pages scroll instead of being squeezed into one screen. Eight indicators
    # do not fit on a phone at any useful size, and a chart squashed to fit is
    # worse than one you scroll to.
    scrolling: true
    theme: [default, fedscreen.scss]
    nav-buttons:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/vibey19/fedscreen
        aria-label: Source code on GitHub
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup

# The dashboard reads one file: data/combined/indicators.csv. It cannot reach a
# site database, and that is the point. Everything individual was left behind
# at the site before this file was written.
#
# Quarto runs this document from the folder it sits in, so work out where the
# project root is rather than assuming. This is the same idiom the tests use.
project_root <- normalizePath(
  if (file.exists("../data/combined/indicators.csv")) ".." else "."
)

# Both files source each other's dependencies with paths relative to the
# project root, so step into it to load them and step back out again.
local({
  previous <- setwd(project_root)
  on.exit(setwd(previous), add = TRUE)
  source("R/dashboard.R")        # reading, picking rows, formatting numbers
  source("dashboard/charts.R")   # the three charts
})

indicators <- read_indicators(
  file.path(project_root, "data", "combined", "indicators.csv")
)

headline <- headline_level(indicators)
by_year  <- year_level(indicators)
by_sex   <- group_level(indicators, "sex")
by_age   <- group_level(indicators, "age_group")
```

## Row

::: {.notice}
**All of this data is simulated.** Three fictional screening sites, invented
parameters, no real people and no real Finnish figures. See
[About the data](#about-the-data).
:::

```

```{r}
#| title: "What this shows"

# A card of plain text, written from the numbers rather than typed out, so it
# cannot drift away from them when the simulation changes.
participation <- headline[headline$indicator == "participation", ]
completion <- headline[headline$indicator == "colonoscopy_completion", ]

lowest <- participation$site[which.min(participation$estimate)]
worst_completion <- completion$site[which.min(completion$estimate)]

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "The three sites were given different parameters on purpose, so there is ",
  "something to compare.\n\n",
  "- Participation runs from **",
  format_estimate(min(participation$estimate), "proportion", FALSE), "** at ",
  lowest, " to **",
  format_estimate(max(participation$estimate), "proportion", FALSE), "** at ",
  participation$site[which.max(participation$estimate)], ".\n",
  "- Colonoscopy completion is weakest at ", worst_completion, " (**",
  format_estimate(min(completion$estimate), "proportion", FALSE),
  "**), which in a real programme is the kind of gap a quality review would ",
  "look at first, because a positive test with no colonoscopy after it is a ",
  "missed chance rather than a reassurance.\n",
  "- Every interval is a 95% confidence interval, written by hand in ",
  "`R/indicators.R`: Wilson for percentages, exact Poisson for rates.\n\n",
  "Where a count behind a cell was between 1 and 4 it is shown as ",
  "*suppressed*, never as a zero."
))
```

## Row {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: "Zero is not suppressed"

# This one table is the clearest thing on the dashboard: in the bottom row,
# Site B publishes a true zero while Site A and Site C are suppressed. Showing
# a suppressed cell as 0 would have merged the two.
knitr::kable(
  breakdown_table(by_age, "cancer_detection_rate"),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  caption = "Cancer detection rate per 1,000 screened, by age group."
)
```

```{r}
#| title: "What is missing, and why"

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "Suppression bites hardest exactly where you would most like the detail. ",
  "The youngest and oldest age bands are small in these simulated ",
  "programmes, and a rare finding in a small group gives a count of 1 to 4, ",
  "which must not be published.\n\n",
  "By sex: ", suppressed_note(by_sex), "\n\n",
  "By age group: ", suppressed_note(by_age), "\n\n",
  "Suppressed cells are left off the charts and shown as the word ",
  "`suppressed` in the tables. They are never shown as zero. Look at the ",
  "75 to 79 row of the table in the previous tab: Site B really did find no ",
  "cancers in that age band, so it publishes 0.0, while Site A and Site C ",
  "each found between 1 and 4 and so publish nothing. Zero is a finding. ",
  "Suppressed means nobody is allowed to tell you."
))
```

# About the data {#about-the-data}

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "The data is simulated"

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "Every individual record behind this dashboard was generated by ",
  "`R/simulate.R` from a fixed random seed. There are no real people in it ",
  "and no real screening programme. The three sites are called Site A, Site B ",
  "and Site C, and their parameters (participation, test positivity, ",
  "colonoscopy completion, how often each finding occurs) were invented to ",
  "make the sites different enough to compare.\n\n",
  "**The numbers on this page are not Finnish statistics, or anybody else's. ",
  "They must not be quoted as real.** Every parameter used is written out in ",
  "`docs/assumptions.md`, which also says plainly that the parameters are ",
  "invented rather than taken from a published source.\n\n",
  "What is real is the method: the indicator definitions, the confidence ",
  "intervals, the suppression rule and the federated structure are the ones ",
  "you would use on real registry data."
))
```

```{r}
#| title: "How the federated part works"

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "Each site holds its own individual-level data in its own database, and ",
  "that data is not allowed to leave. So the same R pipeline runs at each ",
  "site, on the site's own machine, and exports only counts:\n\n",
  "```\n",
  "  at each site          |   centrally\n",
  "  --------------------- | ---------------------\n",
  "  site database         |\n",
  "    -> local pipeline   |\n",
  "    -> aggregate CSV   -->  schema check\n",
  "                        |     -> combined table\n",
  "                        |       -> this dashboard\n",
  "```\n\n",
  "Everything left of the CSVs stays at the site. The central step reads only ",
  "those three aggregate files, so no individual record ever reaches it, and ",
  "this dashboard is one step further out again: it reads a single combined ",
  "CSV of ", format(nrow(indicators), big.mark = ","), " rows and nothing ",
  "else.\n\n",
  "Before anything is combined, each file is checked against a schema both ",
  "sides agreed in advance (`schema/aggregate_schema.yml`): the columns, the ",
  "types, the allowed values, and rules such as *no count between 1 and 4 may ",
  "ever appear* and *a suppressed row carries no estimate*. A file that breaks ",
  "any of them is refused, with a message naming the column, the value and ",
  "the row. Nothing is quietly tidied up."
))
```

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "The suppression rule"

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "Any cell with a count between 1 and ", SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD - 1,
  " is suppressed before a site exports anything. The count is replaced by ",
  "nothing, the row is flagged, and anything computed from it (the estimate ",
  "and both confidence limits) is removed too. A count of 0 is published, ",
  "because it does not identify anybody, and so is any count of ",
  SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD, " or more.\n\n",
  "This is what registries do to stop someone working backwards from a ",
  "published table to a person. In a programme of this size, an age group ",
  "with three cancers in it is a group where somebody who knows one of those ",
  "three people could work out the rest.\n\n",
  "It is enforced in three places: the site applies it, the site refuses to ",
  "write its export if a small count survived, and the central step checks ",
  "the whole rule again before combining. The site is where the mistake ",
  "happens and the centre is where it becomes public, so it is worth ",
  "checking twice. The rule is written up in `docs/assumptions.md`, ",
  "including what it does not do (there is no secondary suppression here)."
))
```

```{r}
#| title: "Suppressed cells by site"

suppression_summary <- indicators |>
  dplyr::group_by(Site = indicators$site) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Cells = dplyr::n(),
    Suppressed = sum(.data$suppressed),
    `Share suppressed` = paste0(
      formatC(100 * sum(.data$suppressed) / dplyr::n(), format = "f",
              digits = 1), "%"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(suppression_summary, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
             caption = paste("Across all breakdown levels. The combined table",
                             "has", format(nrow(indicators), big.mark = ","),
                             "rows in all."))
```

```{r}
#| title: "Where to look next"

knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "- `docs/indicators.md`: every indicator with its numerator, denominator ",
  "and a one-line plain explanation.\n",
  "- `docs/assumptions.md`: every simulation parameter, and the suppression ",
  "rule in full.\n",
  "- `R/indicators.R`: the Wilson and Poisson intervals, written out rather ",
  "than taken from a package.\n",
  "- `schema/aggregate_schema.yml`: the contract a site exports against.\n\n",
  "Built with R and Quarto. The whole pipeline runs with one command: ",
  "`targets::tar_make()`."
))
```
